project.name: laptop-test-checklist
project.description: BenchCheck is a structured inspection checklist for second-hand laptops. It turns an ad-hoc looks-fine decision into an ordered set of verifiable checks, so defects surface before money changes hands, with offline display and keyboard tests built in.

nodes.name: App.tsx
nodes.summary: Application shell that owns the active tab state, renders the sticky header and tab navigation, mounts the checklist provider, and swaps between splash, checklist, display test, and keyboard test views.
nodes.languageNotes: Tab union type plus conditional rendering; LogoMark is exported for reuse in SummaryBar and SplashPage.

nodes.name: LogoMark
nodes.summary: Exported SVG logo component showing the BenchCheck frame-break mark, colored through currentColor and sized by className.

nodes.name: Header
nodes.summary: Sticky header with logo button returning to splash, tab navigation for checklist and test views, live done/total and failure counters, and the GitHub link.

nodes.name: Shell
nodes.summary: Layout component holding tab state, resetting scroll on tab change, rendering the skip link and header, and mounting the active page plus the hidden print report.

nodes.name: App

nodes.name: PrintReport.tsx

nodes.name: SplashPage.tsx

nodes.languageNotes: Interactive demo state cycles each row through pending/pass/fail; keyboard listeners mirror the real key-test preview.

nodes.name: SplashPage

nodes.name: SectionRail.tsx

nodes.name: checklist.ts
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for all checklist content: ten sections with 65 inspection items, section metadata and icons, plus derived item totals and the priority-sorted quick-pass item list.
nodes.languageNotes: Content-only module: exports typed constant arrays and derives QUICK_ITEMS by filtering on an optional numeric priority field.

nodes.name: ChecklistPage.tsx
nodes.summary: Main checklist view: device model input, summary bar, full/quick mode switch, print action, section rail and section bands, plus the brutalist quick-pass deck and failures panel.
nodes.languageNotes: Injects page-scoped CSS keyframes via a style tag and gates the quick-pass layout on checklist mode.

nodes.name: EmptyState

nodes.name: ChecklistPage

nodes.name: Dockerfile

nodes.name: build

nodes.name: sws

nodes.name: static-debian12
nodes.summary: Distroless nonroot runtime stage that copies the static-web-server binary and the built dist directory, then exposes port 8080.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Docker build context exclusions that keep node_modules, dist, git metadata, logs, and markdown out of the image build.

tour.title: Product Overview
tour.description: Start with PRODUCT.md, the product brief for BenchCheck: a buyer-side instrument for inspecting a used laptop before purchase, with a short quick pass and a full 65-item pass. AGENTS.md then documents the Bun/React/Tailwind stack, locked design rules, and file structure that the rest of the tour follows. README.md is only the default Vite template text, so treat it as setup boilerplate rather than product documentation.

tour.title: Browser Bootstrap
tour.description: The app starts from index.html, which provides the React root element and full SEO metadata, including Open Graph tags and SoftwareApplication JSON-LD. It loads src/main.tsx, which imports the Geist fonts and global stylesheet before mounting App inside StrictMode. Together these files show the whole path from static HTML to a running React tree, with no server involved.

tour.title: App Shell and Tabs
tour.description: App.tsx is the top-level shell and the highest fan-out file in the project. It owns the active tab, renders the sticky header with the frame-break LogoMark, mounts ChecklistProvider, and swaps between splash, checklist, display test, and keyboard test views. Because every page is imported here, this file is the map of the app's navigation.

tour.title: Domain Types
tour.description: types.ts defines the shared vocabulary the rest of the codebase compiles against: checklist sections, individual check items, the pending/pass/fail status union, and the icon component contract. It has high fan-in precisely because it holds no logic, only contracts. Read it before the content and state layers so the later types make sense.

tour.title: Checklist Content
tour.description: src/data/checklist.ts is the single source of truth for the inspection itself: ten sections with 65 items, section metadata and icons, derived totals, and the priority-sorted quick-pass list. Content lives here rather than in components, so changing what BenchCheck asks means editing this one file. Each group marks one item with a priority score that defines the 30-45 minute quick pass.

tour.title: State and Persistence
tour.description: store.tsx is the most depended-on file in the project, holding full and quick mode statuses, failure reasons, and laptop metadata in React context. It persists each slice to localStorage under mode-scoped keys and exposes cycle(id) plus derived counts for the active mode. The loader helpers at the top of the file show how saved state is rehydrated on first render.

tour.title: Checklist Screen
tour.description: ChecklistPage.tsx is the main working view, combining the device model input, summary bar, full/quick mode switch, print action, section rail, section bands, and the brutalist quick-pass deck. SummaryBar.tsx sits at the top of that view and turns store counts into done/total progress, pass/fail/remaining stats, a two-step reset, and a rubber-stamp grade seal once every item is checked.

tour.title: Sections and Item Rows
tour.description: These components render the checklist itself. SectionBand.tsx draws a section header with its progress count and maps items into rows, while ItemRow.tsx renders each tri-state checkbox and reveals an inline reason input on failure. SectionRail.tsx provides the sticky desktop index and mobile chip scroller, color-coding each section by completion state.

tour.title: Failures and Print Report
tour.description: FailuresPanel.tsx aggregates every failed item with its recorded reason and an anchor link back to the owning section, returning null when nothing fails. PrintReport.tsx is the hidden print-only article that renders the full or quick report with per-item markers, reasons, a date stamp, and the overall grade. Together they turn live checklist state into something a buyer can act on and keep.

tour.title: Splash Landing
tour.description: SplashPage.tsx is the one-time landing view that tells the BenchCheck story through an interactive demo checklist, a key-press preview, a color-pattern preview, stats, and the section list. It reuses checklist data rather than duplicating content, which is why the tour reaches it after the data and state layers. The header logo returns here on demand.

tour.title: Display Test
tour.description: DisplayTestPage.tsx explains the pixel and backlight defects a buyer should look for, then launches a fullscreen color-surface test with keyboard and on-screen controls. It is one of the few places where pure white, black, red, green, and blue are allowed, because those surfaces are the test patterns rather than decoration. This view covers the screen checks that no checklist row can perform for you.

tour.title: Keyboard Test
tour.description: KeyboardTestPage.tsx is the interactive hardware test: it highlights keys as they register, tracks held state, and reports progress toward the total key count, with a touchpad area alongside. keyboardLayout.ts supplies the ThinkPad 6-row US layout as row definitions plus the arrow cluster and total count. The data file keeps layout geometry out of the page component, so the same test could target another keyboard.

tour.title: Theme and Motion
tour.description: src/index.css is the Tailwind v4 entry stylesheet and the source of the locked dark theme tokens, base styles, print report rules, and custom animations for the bolt strike, grade stamp, hazard stripes, and scanlines. It also holds the prefers-reduced-motion handling that the rest of the UI relies on. Reading it explains why components use the signal/pass/fail color names instead of raw palette classes.

tour.title: Build and Type Configuration
tour.description: package.json declares the Bun scripts for dev, build, lint, typecheck, and preview, plus the React 19, Vite, Tailwind, Phosphor, and Geist dependencies. vite.config.ts wires the React and Tailwind v4 plugins, while the tsconfig files split application and tooling compilation with strict unused checks. This is the toolchain that turns the source into the static bundle deployed next.

tour.title: Container and CI
tour.description: The Dockerfile builds the app in a Bun stage and serves the static dist output from a distroless nonroot image running static-web-server on port 8080, with separate build, sws, and runtime stages. .dockerignore keeps node_modules, dist, git metadata, and markdown out of the build context. The Jenkinsfile closes the loop by typechecking and linting on a Bun agent, then building and pushing the tagged image with Buildah.
